title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 10
paragraphs: Gyges, since he could not avoid it, consented. When Candaules judged it time to rest, he led Gyges into the chamber, and the queen soon followed. Gyges watched her as she came in and laid aside her garments, and when her back was turned as she walked toward the bed, he slipped out from his hiding place and made for the door. But as he went out, she caught sight of him, and understanding what her husband had done, she did not cry out, though she was struck with shame, but pretended she had noticed nothing, intending to take her revenge on Candaules. For among the Lydians, as among most other barbarians, it is a disgrace even for a man to be seen naked.
